newsitem.title: USA: Nasdaq slips as techs run out of steam.
newsitem.headline: Nasdaq slips as techs run out of steam.

text.p: Nasdaq stocks ended lower on Wednesday, ending a string of consecutive record closes.
The Nasdaq Composite fell 7.12 points, to close unofficially at 1250.98, the first time this week the index failed to close at a record high.

The decline was largely due to a fall-off in tech stocks, which found renewed strength after Monday's surprisingly strong earnings report from Intel Corp but stalled when earnings from workstation and server maker Sun Microsystems Inc failed to spur similar enthusiasm.

Sun, which had risen steadily in recent sessions, skidded 6-7/8 to 63-1/8 in its first trading since reporting earnings late Tuesday that just barely beat Wall Street estimates. The shares, Nasdaq's most active, were downgraded by several Wall Street firms early today.
Shares in MEMCO Software Ltd MEMCF.O fared well in their initial day of trading, jumping four points to 19.
Breadth was fairly negative, with losers outpacing winners by about four-to-three on the session. Volume was heavy at 560 million shares.
